$comment: D4 — normative extraction contract for theloopskill-mcp. Machine-readable companion to docs/design/ADR-0004-extraction-strategy-and-failure-semantics.md, beside mcp/runtime-pin.json (D1) and mcp/tool-contracts.json (D3). Every value here was measured against the repo on 2026-07-27, not asserted. A later gate checks this file mechanically.

D4_1_authority.rule: Authority is per SYMBOL, not per section. A tool answering about a symbol reads that symbol's authority and cites it. No symbol has two authorities.

DRY_LIMIT.measured: grep -c DRY_LIMIT over execution-modes.md:306-392 returns 0 — DRY_LIMIT is NOT a member of the §M8 block, despite §M8:395 listing it among the block's four sanctioned omissions and validate.mjs:508-509 registering it as an optional segment OF that block (dead code: never matches).
DRY_LIMIT.consequence: No gate enforces that the three templates carrying `const DRY_LIMIT` (loop-until-dry.workflow.js:90, improvement-loop.workflow.js:98, project-coverage-plan.workflow.js:71) match execution-modes.md:153. All four are byte-identical today by hand, not by check.

agents/items/width/tokens formulae.rule: Returned verbatim as a cited text range with parsed:false. The fence carries Σ and prose clauses ('for a non-verify node') — it is pseudo-code, not JavaScript, and must NEVER be fed to the evaluator. Follows ADR-0003's standards_shelf precedent: a parser limitation surfaced is honest; the same limitation hidden reads as an absence of rules.

routing rationale / worked example.rule: NEVER an answer source. §M4:102 and model-routing.md:14 both already rule execution-modes.md the source and this file the defect on disagreement.

D4_2_locator.rule: A block is located by COORDINATE — (file, headingRegex, fenceLang, ordinal, firstLineRegex) — aborting at the next ^##\s. A content search over the tree is FORBIDDEN.
D4_2_locator.measuredWhy: A naive content search for a fence whose first line is '// Canonical ROUTES block' matches 29 sites in the tree: 27 *.workflow.js templates, execution-modes.md:306 (the one authority), and .claude/skills/loop-skill/references/template-contract.md:34 — which is STALE (its MODE line at :37 is the retired v1.1 two-mode definition, its WIDTH at :41 has no lite branch) and invisible to every gate, since validate.mjs:592 walks *.workflow.js only.
D4_2_locator.reuses: scripts/validate.mjs:446 canonicalBlock() — same walk, so check 5 and the server cannot diverge on what 'the block' is

D4_3_evaluation.rule: EVALUATE the block; never reimplement it. Precedent: validate.mjs:373 evaluates template meta with vm.runInNewContext rather than parsing it.

inputConstruction.rule: MANDATORY: `input` is constructed INSIDE the vm from a JSON literal the server serializes. No host-realm object may cross the boundary.
inputConstruction.measured: With a host-realm object passed in as `input`, `input.constructor.constructor("return typeof process")()` returns "object" — the host realm is reachable — EVEN THOUGH the context sets codeGeneration.strings:false, because that binds the VM's Function, not the host's. Constructing input inside the vm, and passing a null-prototype object, both measured clean.

harvest.rule: Exactly §M8:397's declared invariant core plus WIDTH (which §M8 always carries even though templates may omit it). plannerAgent, fableGateAgent and FABLE_GATE are NOT harvested — they call agent() and log(), which the server does not and must not provide.
harvest.measured: async function bodies referencing unbound agent/log DEFINE cleanly; bodies are not evaluated at definition time.

notASecurityBoundary.statement: The vm isolates the block from the server's own globals. It is NOT a security sandbox — Node's own documentation says so.
notASecurityBoundary.provenanceArgument: §M8 is a law file in the repo the server ships from, held by validate.mjs check 5 and by review. If that ever stops being true, evaluation stops being safe and the decision must be revisited, not patched.

measuredContextProperties.vmRealmFunctionAndEval: EvalError — Code generation from strings disallowed

cost.ruling: evaluate live on every call; ADR-0001's deferral of caching costs nothing on this path

source.kind: first markdown table under the heading

D4_4_crosscheck.labelNormalization:
take text before '
', strip **, trim, split on '/'

aliasMap.$comment: DECLARED, never inferred. An unmapped token is an ERROR, not a skip — a silently-skipped token is how a renamed kind stops being cross-checked while the coverage count still reads 10.

dedupeRowKeysToSet.why: MEASURED CHECKER BUG, not a doc defect: the first draft mapped 'correctness-critical'->gating AND matched the literal 'gating' in the same row label, reporting gating claimed twice. Row labels must be deduped to a set BEFORE counting.

planner@fable.rule: Checked through optsFor({taskType:'planner'}) under {planner:'fable'}, NEVER against ROUTES, and EXCLUDED from the coverage count.
planner@fable.why: execution-modes.md:201 — 'selected by the flag, not by the node'. PLANNER (:312) overrides only opts.model; effort still comes from routeFor('planner').

D4_4_crosscheck.coverageAssertion: every one of the ten ROUTES keys is claimed EXACTLY ONCE across the table

D4_5_failureSemantics.rule: A disagreement is a TOOL-LEVEL ERROR, never a silent winner. The D4.1 authority ladder settles which FILE to fix; it does not license answering from one reading while the other says otherwise.
D4_5_failureSemantics.envelope: extends ADR-0003 §D3.5 — {code, message, fix, details[], fallback}; `fix` is MANDATORY and imperative, per ADR-0002 §D2.4's grammar

structural.behaviour: ok:false / isError:true IN BAND. initialize and tools/list still succeed; the server never dies on a bad document (ADR-0002 degrade-not-die).

semantic.behaviour: ok:false, and error.details[] carries BOTH readings with BOTH citations. Never resolve by precedence at call time.

advisory.behaviour: ok:true. The answer is §M8's. The drift rides in notes[] with both citations.

D4_5_failureSemantics.exampleFix: crosscheck-disagreement -> 'edit execution-modes.md §M3 to match §M8 — §M4:102 makes §M8 the source', NEVER 'ignore §M3'

unknownModeInteraction.measured: The §M8 block itself resolves an UNRECOGNIZED mode SILENTLY to 'balanced' (measured: LITE->balanced, fast->balanced, absent->balanced), exactly as §M9.5:421 warns.
unknownModeInteraction.rule: route_node MUST validate the mode against the advertised enum BEFORE evaluating, and return ADR-0003's unknown_mode error naming the three values. It must never inherit the block's silent fallback.

D4_6_contradictionRuling.theHalfThatMoved: the prose — §M5:156's parenthetical quote and §M6's width(n) rows plus :199

repairsApplied.note: Deletes the second definition of MODE rather than refreshing it, and states the DRY_LIMIT authority split. Refreshing would have restored a copy that drifts again on the next §M8 edit with no gate on it.
optimize -> balanced in the width(n) rows, aligning them with the BAND table twelve lines below
mode='full' -> mode='all-out'; mode='optimize' -> mode='balanced'; 'the optimize band' -> 'the `balanced` band'

deliberatelyNotTouched.why: There `optimize` is the word a HUMAN TYPES as the third answer to the pre-flight question, not a mode value. Renaming it would change a consent contract D4 does not rule on.

D4_6_contradictionRuling.bothReadingsOfM5_156_wereFalse: Read as a claim about the quoted MODE line, the quote is the retired v1.1 two-mode definition. Read as a claim about the DRY_LIMIT line in the fence above it, there is no DRY_LIMIT line in §M8 to be identical to.

gatesAfterRepair.smoke: 26 of 27 — same pre-existing loop-build/v1-conductor planner failure recorded in mcp/runtime-pin.json.gateBaseline
gatesAfterRepair.whyTheRepairIsSafe: smoke.mjs never opens execution-modes.md; validate.mjs reads only §M8 via MODES_DOC (:25). Neither gate reads §M5 or §M6 prose — which is exactly why the drift survived.

E1.name: locate
E1.asserts: heading, fence open, fence close, non-empty, first-line anchor — in that order

E2.name: evaluate
E2.asserts: the block evaluates in the locked context and yields ROUTES

E3.name: invariant core
E3.asserts: MODE, PLANNER, ROUTES, routeFor, optsFor, WIDTH all present; routeFor/optsFor/WIDTH are functions

E4.name: mode vocabulary
E4.asserts: Object.keys(ROUTES) === ['lite','balanced','all-out'] in order; each canonical mode resolves to itself; optimize->balanced and full->all-out

E5.name: kind coverage
E5.asserts: Object.keys(ROUTES[m]) identical for all three modes and equal to the ten canonical keys in order

E6.name: §M3 cross-check
E6.asserts: columns, alias mapping, coverage-exactly-once, cell-by-cell agreement

E7.name: retired vocabulary
E7.mechanism: sha256 CONTENT allowlist, NOT a line-number allowlist
E7.measuredWhy: The first design pinned sanctioned lines by NUMBER; deleting one §M3 row shifted every later line and produced two spurious failures. Hashing the line text is shift-proof.
E7.shrinkOnly: A sanctioned line that DISAPPEARS is not an error — the compat shim shrinking is the intended direction (§M9.6:429). Any NEW or EDITED occurrence of a retired mode VALUE fails.

allowlist.excerpt: A mode is chosen **once per invocation and frozen for that run**
6. **`optimize` and `full` are deprecated aliases, still accepted.**

mutationMatrix.$comment: Every row planted against the real tree and observed firing. The unmutated tree passes E1-E7 (E8 is red by pin, see D4_8).

rows.reportedAs: mode-vocabulary-changed: alias optimize resolves to optimize, pinned balanced

rows.mutation: the stale optimize prose reinstated at :156

mutationMatrix.theTwoRowsTheTaskAskedFor: If §M8 is the half that moves back to the retired vocabulary, E4 fails. If the prose is the half that moves, E7 fails.

D4_8_advisoryThirdCopy.headerIsHalfRenamed: 'optimize effort' means BALANCED effort; 'full effort' means ALL-OUT effort
why: The tie-break is already law twice over: execution-modes.md §M4:102 and model-routing.md:14 both say execution-modes.md is the source and this file is the defect on disagreement.
The fix is an edit to a file D4 does not rule on.
Blocking every route_node call on a pre-existing red would ship a server that never answers — the mistake ADR-0002 §D2.4 already ruled against.
D4_8_advisoryThirdCopy.shrinkOnly: A FOURTH disagreement fails the gate. Repairing any of these three ALSO fails the gate, forcing the pin to shrink rather than rot. Same property as E7's allowlist.

relatedUnfixed.text: a `scout` node moving Haiku 4.5 -> Opus 5 at `high`
relatedUnfixed.note: same class of error, in §M6 prose; NOT repaired because D4 rules only on the optimize/balanced contradiction

D4_9_gateAssertions.$comment: What D4 adds to the golden-query gate, on top of ADR-0003 §D3.9's fifteen.
assertions: No model ID string ('claude-haiku-4-5','claude-sonnet-5','claude-opus-5','claude-fable-5') and no effort literal ('medium','high','xhigh','max') appears anywhere in mcp/server.mjs — every one must be a property of an object the evaluator returned.
The extraction resolves the §M8 block to the byte range pinned in D4_2, and its sha256 matches the pin or the gate reports the drift with both hashes.
E1-E7 pass against the unmutated tree.
Each of the fourteen mutations in D4_7.mutationMatrix, planted in a scratch copy of the tree, produces the stated error code — the gate MUST NOT mutate the repo.
route_node rejects mode:'fast' with unknown_mode BEFORE evaluating, and never returns 'balanced' for it (the block's own silent fallback must not leak).
estimate_phase returns §M6's untagged fence with parsed:false and a citation covering lines 179-197.
A tool asked for the dry threshold cites execution-modes.md:153, NOT §M8.
E8's disagreement set equals D4_8.pinnedDisagreements exactly — more OR fewer fails.
The evaluator's context object has a null prototype and `input` is built inside the vm: assert that a block containing `input.constructor` sees undefined.

D4_10_notRuledHere: Whether model-routing.md:35-43 is repaired, and by whom (D4 rules only that it is advisory and pins its current drift).
execution-modes.md:221's 'at `high`' scout claim, and :229/:244's human-facing `optimize` answer word.
Whether validate.mjs gains a check 9 diffing §M5:153 against the three templates that carry DRY_LIMIT (see D4_1.symbols.DRY_LIMIT.consequence).
Caching, HTTP transport, packaging — deferred by the approved v1 line.
